title: Bullying victim turns pain into purpose, advocates for change - NewsBreak
text:
By Rachel Davis ,
3 hours ago
TYLER, Texas ( KETK )– One high school senior is putting out a call to action for the Elkhart community, bringing her own story of facing bullying to light and encouraging her neighbors and peers to take a stand.
“It was disappointing, that was a big feeling for me,” high school senior Avery Bacon said.
Bacon said she decided to leave school in her last year because bullying became too much.
“It really just started with teasing that all boys do to girls since the beginning of time, and it then grew into not just teasing, and it was being really drawn out and targeted,” Bacon said. “I couldn’t sit in class without being berated with comments.”
Kilgore College athletic director trailblazing a path for women Bacon decided it was best to go from the hallways to homeschooling in the middle of her semester. After stepping away from the constant chaos, she decided to share her story, posting an open letter online calling her community to take action against bullying.
“I really wrote the letter to show that it’s not just teasing, because what if I wasn’t me?” Bacon said. “What if I were a different person who was really, really in a dark place? Because the outcome could have been really tragic and different.”
Bacon shared the heartfelt details of her losses and the years of hard work wasted, hoping to make situations like hers preventable in the future.
“It’s not to call out anyone, it’s not to call out any school, it’s to show these situations that happened that were, for one, easily preventable,” Bacon said.
After publishing her letter, hundreds of people flooded the comment section with words of encouragement, some even sharing their own bullying experiences.
“I was really grateful that I had a community around me that had my back when it felt like nobody did, when it felt like I was by myself,” Bacon said.
Bacon leveraged her social media boom to share the harm it has caused others, creating a platform for people to anonymously share their experiences and continue spreading awareness beyond the Piney Woods.
“I really paired this letter, this experience, and turned the hurt into something helpful that I can bring to not only the community, but I’m competing in nationals representing Texas at NAM nationals in November, and so I want to bring it nationwide,” Bacon said
